construct: Heterozygous loss-of-function CASR variants raise the extracellular-calcium set point required to suppress parathyroid hormone secretion and increase renal tubular calcium reabsorption, producing mild lifelong hypercalcemia with inappropriately normal or mildly elevated PTH and relative hypocalciuria.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Familial asymptomatic mild hypercalcemia with nonsuppressed PTH, low urinary calcium, and CASR loss of function is FHH1 caused by a raised calcium-sensing set point and increased renal calcium reabsorption.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the closest clinical alternative, but familial mild hypercalcemia plus hypocalciuria and an explicit heterozygous CASR loss-of-function variant uniquely support FHH1. CaSR gain of function and PTH resistance give opposite calcium phenotypes.
